It starts in its unique\\nstationary distribution pi. No rates, pi values, topology, or |S| are supplied.\\nAll state variables are even under physical time reversal; systems with odd\\nvariables or time-dependent driving need a different explicitly supplied reversal.\\nThe dimensionless stationary EP rate is\\n\\n    sigma(Q) = sum_{i!=j} pi_i q_ij log(pi_i q_ij / (pi_j q_ji)).  (C1)\\n\\nObservation is a fixed deterministic map h:S->A into a fixed finite alphabet A,\\npossibly many-to-one. We allow time-grid sampling, jump records, or measurable\\nfurther coarsenings of a fixed-duration observed path, provided the observation\\ncommutes with reversal. For a record Z of duration T, the observer knows a measurable\\ninvolution R with Z(X reversed)=R Z(X). Records must retain physical duration;\\nsample count or jump count is not silently substituted for elapsed time.\\nMemoryless stochastic sensing is also allowed if its conditional channel commutes\\nwith reversal and introduces no extra autonomous dissipative dynamics. The proof\\nbelow only needs deterministic masking.\\n\\nFor stationary full microscopic paths, the forward/reversed path likelihood ratio is\\n\\n    log(pi_{X_0}/pi_{X_T}) + sum_jumps log(q_forward/q_backward).\\n\\nThe holding-time factors cancel. Taking its expectation gives exactly T sigma(Q):\\nthe stationary endpoint term has expectation zero, and expected edge-jump counts are\\nT pi_i q_ij. The pi terms in (C1) likewise sum to zero by stationarity. Hence data\\nprocessing gives the finite-duration identity/inequality\\n\\n    D(P_Z || R P_Z) <= T sigma(Q). R P means\\nthe pushforward of the same stationary forward-record law by the known reversal.\\n\\n2. The one-extra-state obstruction, with complete proof\\n------------------------------------------------------\\nModel class M is closed under adding one microscopic state whose observation label\\nduplicates an existing label. This is true for unrestricted finite hidden topology\\nand state count. Take any base model A=(Q,pi,h) in M with sigma_A>0, any state a in S,\\nand any w in (0,1), epsilon>0. Append state b, leave all old off-diagonal rates as\\nbefore, and set\\n\\n    q'_ab=epsilon,\\n    q'_ba=w pi_a epsilon/(1-w),\\n    q'_ib=q'_bi=0 for i!=a.\\n\\nAdjust the two diagonals to make rows sum to zero, and assign h'(b)=h(a). The new\\nchain is finite, irreducible, and has reciprocal support. Its stationary distribution is\\n\\n    pi'_i=w pi_i for i in S;       pi'_b=1-w.\\n\\nIndeed, old internal stationarity is scaled by w, and the new bridge has equal\\nstationary flows pi'_a q'_ab=pi'_b q'_ba=w pi_a epsilon. The bridge contributes\\nzero EP, and every old edge contributes w times its former EP. Therefore\\n\\n    sigma(Q')=w sigma_A.                                      (N2)\\n\\nCouple a path of the base chain started at pi with a path of Q' started inside S.\\nUntil the first bridge jump, the old jump rates agree. Conditional on a base path,\\nthe probability that the independent bridge clock never fires is\\n\\n    exp[-epsilon integral_0^T 1{X_t=a} dt] >= exp(-epsilon T).\\n\\nThe stationary probability of starting inside S is w. Thus for every measurable\\nevent E in the observed-record space, including independent algorithm randomization,\\n\\n    P_Q'(E) >= w exp(-epsilon T) P_A(E).                       (N3)\\n\\nSuppose the same procedure L_T satisfies P_Q{L_T<=sigma(Q)}>=1-alpha for every\\nQ in M. Let E={L_T>=c sigma_A}, choose w<c, and use (N2). Then E is a coverage\\nfailure for Q', giving\\n\\n    w exp(-epsilon T) P_A(E) <= alpha.\\n\\nLet epsilon decrease to zero, then w increase to c. This proves (N1).\\nThe limiting model itself need not be irreducible: every positive epsilon used in\\nthe argument is admissible, so the proof uses no inadmissible model as a premise.\\n\\nFixed-time consequence: an honest sequence L_T over M cannot converge in probability\\nto sigma_A at any driven base A. For c>alpha, convergence would give P_A(E)->1,\\ncontradicting the ceiling alpha/c<1 at every T. This is stronger than saying that\\nthe convergence rate is unknown. The entire pointwise consistency of uniformly\\nhonest bounds fails over this extension-closed class.\\n\\nAnytime consequence: let T_k increase to infinity and assume\\nP_Q{forall k, L_{T_k}<=sigma(Q)}>=1-alpha for every Q. Apply (N3) on the longest\\nfinite prefix to E_N={there exists k<=N: L_{T_k}>=c sigma_A}. The same limiting\\nargument bounds P_A(E_N) by alpha/c; continuity from below gives the bound for\\nthe event with any finite k. No deterministic duration can evade this result.\\n\\nn-replicate consequence: for n independent stationary trajectories of finite durations\\nT_1,...,T_n, the no-bridge lower domination is\\nw^n exp[-epsilon sum_i T_i] P_A^{replicates}(E). Consequently\\n\\n    P_A^{replicates}{L>=c sigma_A} <= min(1, alpha/c^n).        (N4)\\n\\nTo attain power p>alpha, it is necessary that\\nn >= ceil(log(p/alpha)/(-log c)). For alpha=.05,p=.95,c=.9 this is 28 independent\\nstationary starts, regardless of each finite trajectory's duration. Splitting one\\ntrajectory into 28 segments does not supply 28 stationary independent starts.\\nNo attainability theorem for this replica floor is claimed.\\n\\nScope: known fixed hidden-state count excluding this extension, a certified mixing\\nbound, interventions, nonstationary active-state initialization, or a known microscopic\\ngenerator are outside (N1)'s contract. Those may permit useful inference. The added\\nstate is hidden even when the base record distinguishes every base state: its label\\nduplicates a, so the extension does not enlarge the observation alphabet.\\n\\nStronger dormant-copy variant: an independent blind reconstruction supplied a\\nrefinement, checked here after that reconstruction was frozen. For each old state i\\nappend a dormant copy b_i with h(b_i)=h(i), stationary weights w pi_i and (1-w) pi_i,\\nbridge rates q_{i,b_i}=epsilon(1-w)/w and q_{b_i,i}=epsilon, and no internal dormant\\nedges. The full chain remains irreducible; all bridges are detailed-balanced; EP is\\nexactly w sigma_A. The visible one-time stationary distribution is EXACTLY the same\\nas the base model's, and the active no-bridge submeasure is exactly\\nw exp[-epsilon(1-w)T/w] P_A. Thus (N1)-(N4) also hold for an extension-closed class\\nin which the exact visible stationary marginal is supplied to the estimator. The\\none-extra-state construction is sufficient without that extra restriction; the\\ndormant-copy version charges |S| added hidden states to preserve the marginal.\\n\\n3. Repaired adaptive confidence sequence\\n---------------------------------------\\nAt stage i choose, using earlier records only, a physical duration T_i>0, a\\nreversal-compatible coarsening/observable, an antisymmetric critic f_i(Rz)=-f_i(z),\\nand a deterministic or predictable positive clip B_i with |f_i|<=B_i. It starts in its unique
stationary distribution pi. No rates, pi values, topology, or |S| are supplied.
All state variables are even under physical time reversal; systems with odd
variables or time-dependent driving need a different explicitly supplied reversal.
The dimensionless stationary EP rate is

    sigma(Q) = sum_{i!=j} pi_i q_ij log(pi_i q_ij / (pi_j q_ji)).  (C1)

Observation is a fixed deterministic map h:S->A into a fixed finite alphabet A,
possibly many-to-one. We allow time-grid sampling, jump records, or measurable
further coarsenings of a fixed-duration observed path, provided the observation
commutes with reversal. For a record Z of duration T, the observer knows a measurable
involution R with Z(X reversed)=R Z(X). Records must retain physical duration;
sample count or jump count is not silently substituted for elapsed time.
Memoryless stochastic sensing is also allowed if its conditional channel commutes
with reversal and introduces no extra autonomous dissipative dynamics. The proof
below only needs deterministic masking.

For stationary full microscopic paths, the forward/reversed path likelihood ratio is

    log(pi_{X_0}/pi_{X_T}) + sum_jumps log(q_forward/q_backward).

The holding-time factors cancel. Taking its expectation gives exactly T sigma(Q):
the stationary endpoint term has expectation zero, and expected edge-jump counts are
T pi_i q_ij. The pi terms in (C1) likewise sum to zero by stationarity. Hence data
processing gives the finite-duration identity/inequality

    D(P_Z || R P_Z) <= T sigma(Q).                             (C2)

This CTMC derivation is supplied here, rather than treating Ehrich's discrete-time
long-path rate formula as an unexplained finite-duration CTMC theorem. R P means
the pushforward of the same stationary forward-record law by the known reversal.

2. The one-extra-state obstruction, with complete proof
------------------------------------------------------
Model class M is closed under adding one microscopic state whose observation label
duplicates an existing label. This is true for unrestricted finite hidden topology
and state count. Take any base model A=(Q,pi,h) in M with sigma_A>0, any state a in S,
and any w in (0,1), epsilon>0. Append state b, leave all old off-diagonal rates as
before, and set

    q'_ab=epsilon,
    q'_ba=w pi_a epsilon/(1-w),
    q'_ib=q'_bi=0 for i!=a.

Adjust the two diagonals to make rows sum to zero, and assign h'(b)=h(a). The new
chain is finite, irreducible, and has reciprocal support. Its stationary distribution is

    pi'_i=w pi_i for i in S;       pi'_b=1-w.

Indeed, old internal stationarity is scaled by w, and the new bridge has equal
stationary flows pi'_a q'_ab=pi'_b q'_ba=w pi_a epsilon. The bridge contributes
zero EP, and every old edge contributes w times its former EP. Therefore

    sigma(Q')=w sigma_A.                                      (N2)

Couple a path of the base chain started at pi with a path of Q' started inside S.
Until the first bridge jump, the old jump rates agree. Conditional on a base path,
the probability that the independent bridge clock never fires is

    exp[-epsilon integral_0^T 1{X_t=a} dt] >= exp(-epsilon T).

The stationary probability of starting inside S is w. Thus for every measurable
event E in the observed-record space, including independent algorithm randomization,

    P_Q'(E) >= w exp(-epsilon T) P_A(E).                       (N3)

Suppose the same procedure L_T satisfies P_Q{L_T<=sigma(Q)}>=1-alpha for every
Q in M. Let E={L_T>=c sigma_A}, choose w<c, and use (N2). Then E is a coverage
failure for Q', giving

    w exp(-epsilon T) P_A(E) <= alpha.

Let epsilon decrease to zero, then w increase to c. This proves (N1).
The limiting model itself need not be irreducible: every positive epsilon used in
the argument is admissible, so the proof uses no inadmissible model as a premise.

Fixed-time consequence: an honest sequence L_T over M cannot converge in probability
to sigma_A at any driven base A. For c>alpha, convergence would give P_A(E)->1,
contradicting the ceiling alpha/c<1 at every T. This is stronger than saying that
the convergence rate is unknown. The entire pointwise consistency of uniformly
honest bounds fails over this extension-closed class.

Anytime consequence: let T_k increase to infinity and assume
P_Q{forall k, L_{T_k}<=sigma(Q)}>=1-alpha for every Q. Apply (N3) on the longest
finite prefix to E_N={there exists k<=N: L_{T_k}>=c sigma_A}. The same limiting
argument bounds P_A(E_N) by alpha/c; continuity from below gives the bound for
the event with any finite k. No deterministic duration can evade this result.

n-replicate consequence: for n independent stationary trajectories of finite durations
T_1,...,T_n, the no-bridge lower domination is
w^n exp[-epsilon sum_i T_i] P_A^{replicates}(E). Consequently

    P_A^{replicates}{L>=c sigma_A} <= min(1, alpha/c^n).        (N4)

To attain power p>alpha, it is necessary that
n >= ceil(log(p/alpha)/(-log c)). For alpha=.05,p=.95,c=.9 this is 28 independent
stationary starts, regardless of each finite trajectory's duration. Splitting one
trajectory into 28 segments does not supply 28 stationary independent starts.
No attainability theorem for this replica floor is claimed.

Scope: known fixed hidden-state count excluding this extension, a certified mixing
bound, interventions, nonstationary active-state initialization, or a known microscopic
generator are outside (N1)'s contract. Those may permit useful inference. The added
state is hidden even when the base record distinguishes every base state: its label
duplicates a, so the extension does not enlarge the observation alphabet.

Stronger dormant-copy variant: an independent blind reconstruction supplied a
refinement, checked here after that reconstruction was frozen. For each old state i
append a dormant copy b_i with h(b_i)=h(i), stationary weights w pi_i and (1-w) pi_i,
bridge rates q_{i,b_i}=epsilon(1-w)/w and q_{b_i,i}=epsilon, and no internal dormant
edges. The full chain remains irreducible; all bridges are detailed-balanced; EP is
exactly w sigma_A. The visible one-time stationary distribution is EXACTLY the same
as the base model's, and the active no-bridge submeasure is exactly
w exp[-epsilon(1-w)T/w] P_A. Thus (N1)-(N4) also hold for an extension-closed class
in which the exact visible stationary marginal is supplied to the estimator. The
one-extra-state construction is sufficient without that extra restriction; the
dormant-copy version charges |S| added hidden states to preserve the marginal.

3. Repaired adaptive confidence sequence
---------------------------------------
At stage i choose, using earlier records only, a physical duration T_i>0, a
reversal-compatible coarsening/observable, an antisymmetric critic f_i(Rz)=-f_i(z),
